paper.title_en: Squeezing-assisted Fisher-ridge operation in a nonlinear non-Hermitian gyroscope
paper.abstract_en: Non-Hermitian gyroscopes can exhibit enhanced spectral response near mode coalescence, but modal nonorthogonality and noise amplification prevent eigenvalue splitting alone from establishing a metrological advantage. We study a Kerr-nonlinear twin-resonator gyroscope including Sagnac splitting, inter-resonator coupling, Kerr nonlinearity, intrinsic loss, and vacuum noise. The nonlinear mean-field flow, frozen-state effective operator, and full Jacobian are treated separately. No exact nonlinear exceptional point is found in the investigated stable domain; instead, a minimum-defectiveness ridge appears where eigenvalue and eigenvector coalescence indicators are jointly minimized. This ridge remains distinct from the continuity-regularized Fisher ridge, while the strict pointwise Fisher optimum is defined separately. Coherent Fisher-ridge operation provides a modest improvement over the minimum-defectiveness path. With score-matched squeezing at <math altimg="si1.svg" display="inline" id="d1e861"><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mo><mn>3.00</mn></mrow></math> and <math altimg="si268.svg" display="inline" id="d1e871"><mrow><mi>η</mi><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mo><mn>0.998</mn></mrow></math>, the analytic score-channel benchmark gives a <math altimg="si3.svg" display="inline" id="d1e881"><mrow><mn>14.95</mn><mo>×</mo></mrow></math> resolution gain, while full-covariance implementable homodyne detection gives <math altimg="si4.svg" display="inline" id="d1e890"><mrow><mn>14.42</mn><mo>×</mo></mrow></math> for the best single-mode configuration and <math altimg="si5.svg" display="inline" id="d1e898"><mrow><mn>7.90</mn><mo>×</mo></mrow></math> for the best two-mode configuration on the predefined search grid. Independent multichannel Monte Carlo validation and stability, loss, bandwidth, and fixed-calibration analyses delimit the regime in which the squeezing-assisted advantage persists. The results therefore provide a theoretical design target rather than a demonstrated practical gyroscope.
